newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond restrained at 91.920.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond restrained at 91.920.

text.p: *Australian bonds are expected to show an easier bias at the opening after a weak U.S. Treasury market brought a local rally to an abrupt halt in after hours trading.
*The 10-year bond contract touched a high of 91.920 in SYCOM, a level that is expected to prove the peak for now.
Australian bonds are expected to show an easier bias at the opening after a weak U.S. Treasury market brought a local rally to an abrupt halt in after hours trading on Friday.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM at 91.860 compared with Friday's 91.905 open outcry close and after touching a high of 91.920.
This peak represents the top line of a one-month descending channel and is likely to prove the peak for now, while the downside should find initial support at 91.850, analysts said.
U.S. Treasuries weakened after Friday's March labour force report suggested that the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates again in May.

Although non-farm payrolls growth was moderate at 175,000, the unemployment rate dipped to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent and average hourly earnings rose by 0.4 percent to a seven-year high of 4.0 percent year-on-year.
The U.S. 30-year bond yield ended at 7.12 percent against 7.07 percent on Thursday and having touch 7.15 percent at one stage, its highest level since July 1996.
Australia's own labour force report is due on Thursday, which is expected to be the key event for the market this week unless the long awaited decision on the "living wage" claim finally emerges.
A prelude to the jobs data will be the March ANZ job advertisments series at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) this morning.
